newsitem.title: USA: New home sales jump 14.2 percent in November.
newsitem.headline: New home sales jump 14.2 percent in November.

text.p: Sales of new homes rose at the fastest level in nearly four years in November, the Commerce Department said on Tuesday, as relatively benign interest rates attracted buyers across the country.
The department said new home sales rose 14.2 percent to a seasonally-adjusted annual rate of 772,000 after being a downwardly revised 676,000 in October.
The department had originally estimated the October sales at 714,000. The November rise was much higher than Wall Street estimates, which had seen home sales at 731,000.
The strength in sales came from all regions, led by a 40.3 percent rise in the Northeast.
Sales were up 16 percent in the Midwest, 11.5 percent in the West and 10.2 percent in the South.

On Monday the National Association of Realtors reported a respectable 1.8 percent rise in the sales of existing homes last month to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 4.04 million. Compared with a year ago, the resale pace was up 1 percent.
The activity is being helped by relatively attractive mortgage rates.
The Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp. said the national average commitment rate of 30-year, conventional, fixed-rate mortgages fell to 7.62 percent in November from 7.92 percent in October.
The strong new home sales come as the U.S. economy is in its sixth year of expansion, with unemployment at very low levels and inflation seemingly under tight control.
New home sales rose at 16.6 percent in April 1993.
